chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Rabi', from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a bed in which is the gold, is it correct to keep it in the house? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was of gold, so no, and if it was the water of the gold, so there is no problem'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep furniture decorated with gold in the house according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on keeping a bed (*sarir*) adorned with gold, distinguishing between solid gold, which is impermissible to retain, and 'water of gold' (gold-plated or coated), which is permissible. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *mithl* (substance) versus *zayn* (ornament), emphasizing that the prohibition targets the accumulation of precious metal as wealth rather than its use for aesthetic decoration. The ruling underscores the principle that modesty in adornment is encouraged, provided the material does not constitute significant stored wealth.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his fatgher, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Rabi’e, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a bed in which is the gold, is it correct to keep it in the house?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was of gold, so no, but if it was the water of the gold (gold-coated), so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, wore the ring on his left hand which was of gold then he appeared among people who continued staring at it. He (the Messenger of Allah) placed his right hand on the pinky (little finger) of his left hand until he returned home; then threw it and did not wear it again.’” From abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a narration, similar to the above Hadith, is also made by a number of our people from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha’, from al-Muthanna’, from Hatim ibn ’Isma‘il.
